title: five minutes with ... dj katovl menovsky
summary: DJ Katovl Menovsky shares his perspective on Kreuzberg, addressing its reputation, gentrification, and tourism.

titles: five minutes with ... dj katovl menovsky
blocks.markdown:
## five minutes with ... dj katovl menovsky

We test fit Kreuzberg's "Wohnmeisterin" and were shaped here. What do you say to the repeating image? From ghetto to mainstream, or not?

I have never seen my home district as a ghetto. Certainly, I came into contact with violence and criminality, but which average person doesn't? Kreuzberg has shaped me more in the sense that I try to distance myself from stereotypes and clichés, even if it's not always easy. I view the current increase in popularity in Kreuzberg with mixed feelings. The rich, newly arrived residents are already getting on our nerves, but there is also a lot of envy and stereotypes on our part, I openly and gladly admit that. As for tourists, it's similar. There isn't just one type of tourist. Of course, there are the stereotypical English party-goers and pubescent school trips from Montego Bay, but one should never forget the many interesting artists from whom the district benefits.
